close_reason: Added #[derive(Clone, Debug)] to HttpCrlFetcher<F> and HttpOcspFetcher<F> stubs, matching the CrlChecker/OcspChecker pattern. Derive macro adds the appropriate where F: Clone/Debug bounds.
description:
Pass 2 idiom finding under epic PKIX-qwzx.

`pkix-revocation-http/src/lib.rs:95` (`HttpCrlFetcher<F>`) and line 125
(`HttpOcspFetcher<F>`) declare structs with no `#[derive(...)]` attribute:

```rust
#[cfg(feature = \"crl\")]
#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = \"crl\")))]
#[allow(dead_code)] // fields used once HttpCrlFetcher is implemented
pub struct HttpCrlFetcher<F> {
    fetcher: F,
    now_unix: u64,
}
```

Idiomatic Rust for a generic struct intended to be wrapped around a user-supplied
type is to derive `Debug, Clone` with a per-trait bound on `F`. Even without a
Debug bound on `F`, the struct authors should at least add:

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]   // or Debug, Clone — bound: where F: Debug (Clone)
```

The `#[derive(Debug)]` macro expansion already adds `where F: Debug` for the
generic param, so the impl is conditional on the user's `F` supporting it.
This is the same pattern used by `CrlChecker<V>` in `pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:93`
(`#[derive(Clone, Debug)]`) and by `OcspChecker<V>` in `pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:67`.

This is a stub crate (functionality not yet implemented), so this is a P4
cosmetic gap — but it's the same idiom observed elsewhere in the workspace
that was not applied uniformly.

Fix: add `#[derive(Debug, Clone)]` to both structs, matching the pattern in
`pkix-revocation::CrlChecker`.

Locations:
- `pkix-revocation-http/src/lib.rs:92-98` (`HttpCrlFetcher`)
- `pkix-revocation-http/src/lib.rs:122-128` (`HttpOcspFetcher`)
title: (IDIOM) P4: HttpCrlFetcher and HttpOcspFetcher lack any derive (no Debug) in pkix-revocation-http stub
